nodes.title: Pyber's conjecture for $\mathrm{PSL}(2, p)$ holds

nodes.summary: This proposition states that there is a natural number $N$ such that $p \le N$ for every prime $p$ for which the group $G = \mathrm{PSL}(2, p)$, the quotient of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$ by its center, has a subset $S$ closed under conjugation and under inversion with $|S| > |G| / \log_2 |G|$ and $S^2 \ne G$, where $S^2 = \{st : s, t \in S\}$. In other words, only finitely many groups…
nodes.title: Pyber's conjecture for $\mathrm{PSL}(2, p)$ (Kourovka 20.74(b))

nodes.summary: There is no natural number $N$ such that every nonabelian finite simple group $G$ that has a subset $S$ with $g s g^{-1} \in S$ and $s^{-1} \in S$ for all $g \in G$ and $s \in S$, with $|S| > |G| / \log_2 |G|$ and with $S^2 \ne G$, where $S^2 = \{st : s, t \in S\}$, has order $|G| \le N$.
nodes.title: Pyber's conjecture for finite simple groups is false

nodes.summary: This proposition states that there is a natural number $N$ such that every nonabelian finite simple group $G$ that has a subset $S$ closed under conjugation and under inversion with $|S| > |G| / \log_2 |G|$ and $S^2 \ne G$, where $S^2 = \{st : s, t \in S\}$, has order $|G| \le N$. Since there are only finitely many groups of each order, this says that only finitely many such groups exist up to isomorphism.
nodes.title: Pyber's conjecture for finite simple groups (Kourovka 20.74(a))

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has this property when it has a subset $S$ such that $g s g^{-1} \in S$ and $s^{-1} \in S$ for all $g \in G$ and $s \in S$, $S$ has more than $|G| / \log_2 |G|$ elements, and $S^2 = \{st : s, t \in S\}$ is not all of $G$.
